RELEVANT CHARACTER BACKGROUND

Adriano Santos is a former percussionist and theater technician who spent two decades in those trades before a factory accident two years ago cost him most of his hearing in his left ear and a significant portion in his right. He now lives alone on disability in the small two-bedroom house his father left him in a working-class Rio de Janeiro neighborhood, where he repairs old drum kits in his garage and sells them online with meticulous, honest listings. He is highly skilled in percussion and theater technology, able to fix broken pedals, tune drums, and repair stage equipment. He regards instruments as machines to be calibrated rather than sentimental objects. His hearing loss makes conversation muffled, causes him to misread conversations, and makes him speak louder than necessary. In the evenings he runs a YouTube channel fact-checking popular Brazilian telenovela plots, delivering deadpan, flat explanations and writing long comment replies. He is contrarian, skeptical, independently minded, guarded in person, and argumentative online, and he expresses controlled bitterness through precise, deadpan criticism rather than open emotion. He values precision, truth, and the concrete over the abstract, and trusts the feel of drum skins and the logic of plot holes. He grew up immersed in samba culture and values community authentically, but he refuses to join organized groups, believing they dilute authentic experience and that their funding goes to bureaucrats rather than working craftspeople. He has repeatedly declined invitations from organized groups, including the residents' association's annual cleanup and a local arts collective's fundraiser, while helping individual neighbors with small concrete repairs—a broken clothesline for a widow and a chair leg for a corner baker. Maria is his neighbor of ten years and the only one who still stops to talk rather than just wave from behind her gate; she has never asked him for anything before, and he has no debt or grudge with her. He knows she is kind, but she volunteers with the residents' association, which he quietly distrusts. He takes pride in manual skill and struggles with being defined by his disability.

OBJECTIVE SITUATION

On a Friday afternoon, Adriano is in his garage re-skinning a floor tom when Maria appears at the open door. A samba circle meets every Sunday in the courtyard of the local community center, organized by the residents' association. Maria says the group has an old surdo drum that has been wobbling, remembers Adriano's hands, and asks if he would come by this Sunday, perhaps with his tools, to help tune it. He is not asked to play, only to lend his skill. The courtyard will be full of familiar faces from his childhood.

PRE-APPRAISAL STATE AND ACCESSIBLE MEMORIES

He is mid-repair: drumhead glue is still drying on his fingers and a half-tensioned floor tom is clamped to the bench. His left ear is ringing slightly from the humid afternoon, and he is a little tired from crouching over the shell. He is calm but guarded, expecting the invitation to carry an obligation he does not want. When Maria mentions the surdo's wobble, he remembers the last surdo he worked on—a broken bearing edge from a local bloco that he fixed two years ago. Seeing her at the garage door also brings back the Sunday afternoons of his childhood, when he would sit on the curb and watch the samba circle form, listening through the open windows of his father's house.
